name: dispatch_indirect_call_with_argument
description: Loads a function pointer from a fixed offset in a global record and calls it, passing a value built from the low word of D1 scaled by 512 plus A0, then returns zero. Three unnamed routines call it.

name: poll_bit_changes_fifty_times
description: Writes the byte 58 into a field at offset 12 of the record in A1, then polls a global byte while its top bit is set, counting changes of its lowest bit and returning after 50 changes. The facts list the CIA port A register and a custom chip register, but the code only polls the global byte.

name: spin_forever_halt
description: Enters an endless empty loop and never returns, so it halts execution. The facts list a read of the video beam position register, but the code shows no access to it.

name: invoke_routine_pointer_in_a1
description: Calls the routine whose 24-bit address is held in A1, with the top byte masked off, then returns. Five unnamed routines call it.

name: stub_return_only
description: Contains only a return instruction and is entered from outside the static flow in the reference run. It does no work and touches no registers.

description: Contains only a return instruction and is entered from outside the static flow in the reference run. It does no work and touches no registers.

name: configure_custom_chip_enables
description: The pseudo-code could not be produced, so the exact sequence is unconfirmed. The routine has 60 instructions and touches the audio and DMA control, interrupt enable and request, and background colour registers, and it calls five unnamed routines. The register notes say a write with the top bit set enables the matching bits and a write without it disables them.

name: patch_jump_instructions_into_code
description: When a global matches a fixed constant, writes absolute jump and subroutine call instructions at a series of code locations so they redirect to another routine. It then scans a memory range and rewrites each matching four-byte pattern into a subroutine call, so it patches code in place.

name: write_jump_stub_at_pointer
description: Makes a call and, if the result is nonzero, saves it in a global and makes a second call. If the address returned by the second call is non-null, it writes an absolute jump instruction and its 32-bit target into that address. It calls three unnamed routines and one small merge routine.

name: store_word_field_then_return
description: Stores the value 32 into a 16-bit field at offset 156 from A6 and returns the value passed on the stack. The facts list one caller and no hardware registers.

name: search_byte_sequence_in_buffer
description: Slides a window across the first buffer up to the address in A1 and compares each position with the second buffer, counting consecutive matching bytes. It returns as soon as the match count reaches the length in D0, so it searches for a byte sequence of that length.

name: poll_pot_port_button_latch
description: Checks bit 6 of a global flag. When it is clear, it sets the global to a fixed value, stores a status value in a frame field, and sets a shared latch word to a fixed mask if the word was zero; when the bit is set it clears the latch word. The facts list the pot port registers, and the register note names the right and middle buttons.

name: clear_latch_and_set_status
description: Clears the shared 16-bit latch word that the button poll routine uses, then stores the value 32 at offset 156 from A6 and returns a stack value.

name: replace_patterns_with_trap_instructions
description: Scans a memory range forward in steps of two bytes. It replaces one specific four-byte pattern with a trap instruction and a second pattern with a different trap instruction, leaving other data unchanged.

name: pass_through_d0
description: Returns the value already in D0 without changing it and does no other work. Its one caller takes the value as its result.

name: pass_through_d0
description: Returns the value already in D0 without changing it and does no other work. Its one caller takes the value as its result.

name: set_fields_on_marker_byte
description: If the low byte of D0 equals the underscore character, it stores 20 in a 16-bit field and all ones in a byte field of the record addressed by A5, then returns. Otherwise it compares D0 with a global byte and returns. The facts list the CIA interrupt control register, which the code does not touch directly.

name: set_fields_at_matching_record
description: If the low byte of D0 equals the underscore character, it checks A5 against five fixed record addresses and, on a match, stores 20 in a 16-bit field and all ones in a byte field of that record. Otherwise it compares D0 with a global byte and returns. The facts list the CIA interrupt control register.

name: store_default_record_fields
description: Writes 20 into a 16-bit field and all ones into a byte field of the record addressed by A5, with no condition. These are the same two fields that the marker-matching routine sets.

name: store_alternate_record_fields
description: Writes 20 into a 16-bit field and all ones into a byte field of the record addressed by A5, using a different pair of fields from the neighbouring store routine.

name: store_fields_variant_c
description: Writes 20 into a 16-bit field and all ones into a byte field of the record addressed by A5, using a third pair of fields that differs from the other store routines.

name: store_fields_variant_d
description: Writes 20 into a 16-bit field and all ones into a byte field of the record addressed by A5, using a fourth pair of fields that differs from the other store routines.

name: store_fields_variant_e
description: Writes 20 into a 16-bit field and all ones into a byte field of the record addressed by A5, using a fifth pair of fields that differs from the other store routines.

name: copy_global_block_low_memory
description: Copies 240 bytes one at a time from the global data area to the fixed address 512, then returns. The loop has no condition beyond its count.

name: compare_shifted_code_with_global
description: Shifts the low word of D0 right by one bit, XORs the low byte with 127 and compares it with a global byte. Both branches return immediately, so the comparison has no effect.

name: halt_in_endless_loop
description: Enters an endless empty loop and never returns. The facts list a read of the video beam position register, but the code shows no access to it.

name: set_frame_word_all_ones
description: Stores all ones into a 16-bit field at offset 68 from A6 and returns. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: install_fixed_address_jumps
description: Writes absolute jump instructions with target addresses into several fixed locations, making one call between the writes. The facts list five calls in total.

name: load_or_save_global_block
description: When the low byte of D1 is nonzero, copies 48 bytes from the buffer at A0 into the global data area and makes one call. Otherwise, unless a stored signature word equals a fixed value, it copies the global data area out to the buffer.

name: copy_global_block_unless_signed
description: If a stored signature word differs from a fixed value, copies the 48-byte global data area into the buffer at A0. If the signature matches, the buffer is left unchanged and the routine returns.

name: wait_for_flag_then_return
description: Calls one unnamed routine and keeps its result. If a stored word is nonzero, it busy-waits while the top bit of a global byte is set, then returns the saved result. The facts list the CIA port A register, but the code polls only the global byte.

name: forward_call_to_routine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, with no other work. Four unnamed routines call it.

name: store_index_then_call_pointer
description: Stores the character one plus a passed byte into a global, then calls through a function pointer at offset 76 from a stored base record. A non-negative result is returned; otherwise one unnamed routine is called and zero is returned. The referenced text is 'disk.'

name: xor_longs_with_key
description: XORs each 32-bit longword of the buffer at A0 with the value in D7, stepping four bytes at a time for the count in D1. The buffer is modified in place.

name: decompress_lz_stream_into_buffer
description: Decodes a compressed stream into an output buffer. A control byte selects a literal run, a repeat of one byte, or a copy from earlier output, with lengths read from one or two following bytes. It first moves a block of data, then finishes by calling one unnamed routine and one routine through a pointer at offset 32.

name: relay_single_call_unconfirmed
description: The decompiler timed out, so the logic is unconfirmed. The routine has 11 instructions, is called by one unnamed routine, and calls one unnamed routine. No register or text references were recorded.

name: load_scores_block_from_file
description: Sets the stored signature word to a fixed value, then calls through a pointer at offset 36 with a count of 48 and the global data area as the buffer. If that call returns a nonzero count, it caps the count at 48 and calls through a pointer at offset 76, returning the negated result. The referenced text is scores.sav.

name: save_scores_block_to_file
description: Calls through a pointer at offset 56 with a count of 48 and the global data area as the buffer, then returns the negated result. The referenced file name is scores.sav, the same file the load routine uses.

name: set_frame_word_then_call
description: Stores a fixed word value into a 16-bit field at offset 150 from A6, then calls through a function pointer at offset 84 from a stored base record.

name: call_pointer_at_offset_forty
description: Calls through a function pointer at offset 40 from a stored base record and returns, passing no arguments. The facts list one merge routine and no other effects.

name: call_pointer_then_halt
description: Calls through a function pointer at offset 100 from a stored base record, then enters an endless empty loop and never returns.

name: copy_region_after_pointer_call
description: Ors a fixed mask into the byte at A6, calls through a function pointer at offset 100 from a stored base record, then copies a block of bytes from one fixed memory area to another. On each step it writes the low word of a counter to a global.

name: spin_forever_halt
description: Enters an endless empty loop and never returns. The facts list one call, but the code shows only the infinite loop.

name: call_then_copy_block_region
description: Makes one call, then copies a block of bytes from a fixed address to a labelled area, writing the low word of a counter to a global on each step. The facts list writes to the background colour register, which the code does not show directly.

name: encode_run_length_stream
description: Encodes a byte stream into run-length form: literal runs get a count, and repeated bytes get a flagged count, with each run capped at 128 bytes. It stores the final output count through a pointer and calls one unnamed routine and two small routines.

name: encode_run_length_block
description: Encodes a block of source bytes into literal and repeat records, capped at 128 bytes per record. It stores the final output count through a pointer and updates a global with the running count as it goes.

name: write_final_run_record
description: Writes a final run record consisting of a count byte with its top bit set followed by a repeated byte value, then stores the output count through a pointer. One unnamed routine calls it.

name: disable_custom_bits_nine_traps
description: Makes nine trap calls, writes 32767 three times to a global word that the facts link to a custom chip register at offset zero, then makes one more trap call. A value with bit 15 clear disables the matching interrupt and DMA bits, so these writes clear them.

name: disable_custom_bits_eight_traps
description: Makes eight trap calls, writes 32767 three times to a global word that the facts link to a custom chip register at offset zero, then makes one more trap call. A value with bit 15 clear disables the matching interrupt and DMA bits, so these writes clear them.

name: disable_custom_bits_seven_traps
description: Makes seven trap calls, writes 32767 three times to a global word that the facts link to a custom chip register at offset zero, then makes one more trap call. A value with bit 15 clear disables the matching interrupt and DMA bits, so these writes clear them.

name: disable_custom_bits_six_traps
description: Makes six trap calls, writes 32767 three times to a global word that the facts link to a custom chip register at offset zero, then makes one more trap call. A value with bit 15 clear disables the matching interrupt and DMA bits, so these writes clear them.

name: disable_custom_bits_five_traps

name: disable_custom_bits_four_traps

name: disable_custom_bits_three_traps
description: Makes three trap calls, writes 32767 three times to a global word that the facts link to a custom chip register at offset zero, then makes one more trap call. A value with bit 15 clear disables the matching interrupt and DMA bits, so these writes clear them.

name: disable_custom_bits_two_traps

name: disable_custom_bits_one_trap
description: Makes one trap call, writes 32767 three times to a global word that the facts link to a custom chip register at offset zero, then makes one more trap call. A value with bit 15 clear disables the matching interrupt and DMA bits, so these writes clear them.

name: disable_custom_bits_then_trap
description: Writes 32767 three times to a global word that the facts link to a custom chip register at offset zero, then makes one trap call. A value with bit 15 clear disables the matching interrupt and DMA bits, so these writes clear them.

name: call_three_then_write_pair
description: Calls three unnamed routines, then writes 255 and then 32 to a global word, and returns. The facts list an interrupt request register, but the code shows only the writes to the global.

name: step_clamped_level_and_lookup
description: Moves a stored level toward a target by at most one step per call, clamped to a range of minus one to one. It flips the low four bits of the target when a countdown expires, then writes the low nibble of a table entry to a byte, selected by whether the level exceeds seven.

name: scale_colour_entries_by_mode
description: Copies sixteen 16-bit entries from a table into a global buffer, applying a mode-dependent transform: a plain copy, or a right shift by one or two bits with a mask that keeps 3-bit channels. It then stores four plane pointers spaced 32000 bytes apart, offset by 80 bytes when one bit of a global word is clear.

name: scale_colour_entries_variant
description: Performs the same mode-dependent colour copy and plane pointer setup as the routine before it. The decompiled mode test compares a routine address with the mode values, which is a decompiler artefact; the copy itself is the same. The facts list writes to the background colour and vertical position registers, and two unnamed routine calls.

name: configure_display_copper_and_dma
description: The pseudo-code shows only an infinite loop, so the sequence is unconfirmed. The facts list display window, fetch, bitplane modulo and control registers, the copper list pointer and jump, and colour, interrupt, DMA and audio state, with fifteen unnamed routines called.

name: initialise_audio_channel_state
description: Stores three pointers and the value 64 into a block of scratch memory, clears a run of other state words, and writes 15 to a global that the facts link to the audio channel volume registers. It scans a table for its largest word and calls one unnamed routine.

name: advance_audio_channel_records
description: Walks a list of four-longword records for a fixed count, skipping empty ones. For each active record it stores a running value, updates a second field, and advances the running value by a per-record step. When a flag word equals two, it replaces the field with a computed offset of 60 from another value.

name: reset_audio_channel_globals
description: Writes zero to four global words, writes 15 to a global that the facts link to the audio volume registers, and sets a word to all ones. The facts list the audio volume registers and the DMA control register, but the code writes only globals.

name: tick_counter_call_until_six
description: When a flag word is zero, increments a counter. It calls one unnamed routine unless a global byte is zero and the counter has reached six; in that case it resets the counter to zero instead.

name: advance_sequence_step_counter
description: Counts ticks in a per-channel record and, when a tick limit is reached, increments a step counter. At 65 steps it sets a global to 255, advances an index, and reloads a pointer from a table, wrapping the index at a stored limit. It calls unnamed routines before and after the tick logic.

name: select_audio_channel_sample_block
description: Takes a packed command word and, when its high nibble is nonzero, points one of four channel records at a block computed from that nibble. It then writes the pointer, length, period and volume values of that channel to globals. The facts list the audio channel registers for all four channels.

name: apply_channel_effect_command
description: Decodes a command nibble from the top of a value and applies one effect to a channel record: negating the low byte, setting a channel volume, setting a position value, writing a global, or setting or clearing a flag bit. Unrecognised nibbles return unchanged.

name: update_four_channel_state_flags
description: For each of four channels, adds a stored step to a running value and writes it to a global. When a channel's active flag is set, it clears the flag and reloads that channel's data pointer. It then sets active bits for channels that have a pointer and writes the four channel values to globals.

name: write_cia_setup_constants
description: Writes nine constants to global words in sequence, including small mode and count values and two values with the top bit set, then returns. The facts list CIA timer, control and serial registers and the interrupt enable register, but the code shows only the constant writes.

name: issue_two_boot_io_requests
description: Fills two I/O request blocks with a command code, an offset, a length and an address, and issues each through an Amiga OS library call at offset -456. It then loops forever.

name: shift_bit_buffer_with_sentinel
description: Stores the low byte of a longword read just before the input pointer, with the high byte of a parameter, into a word. It returns that longword shifted right one bit with the top bit set, so callers can take bits from it one at a time.

key: Pinball Fantasies (1992)(21st Century)(Disk 1 of 3).adf boot-block load +$CE400 to $030000 (56320 bytes):0:0130

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler marked the body as bad instruction data and cut the control flow to a single error call, so these three instructions are not a verified routine.

name: forward_call_three_routines
description: Calls three unnamed routines in turn and returns, with no other work.

name: store_global_address_then_trap
description: Stores the address of a global into another global, makes one trap call, and returns. The facts list no hardware registers.

name: stub_return_only
description: Contains only a return instruction. The facts list a call from one routine and a touch of a custom chip register at offset zero, but the code does no work.

name: forward_single_call_return
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, with no other work.

name: build_five_entry_pointer_list
description: Fills five 8-byte entries with a pointer split into high and low words, advancing the pointer by 40 bytes per entry, then writes four constants to globals. The facts list the copper list pointer and the vertical position register.

name: wait_for_beam_then_call
description: Repeatedly waits for a fixed vertical beam position in a global, makes one call at that point, and repeats forever because its exit flag is never set. The facts list the vertical position register.

name: call_four_routines_in_turn
description: Calls four unnamed routines in turn, passing no arguments, and returns.

name: call_then_write_display_constants
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then writes eight constants to globals in sequence. The facts list the copper list pointer register, but the code shows only the constant writes.

name: build_four_entry_display_list
description: Fills four 8-byte entries with a pointer split into high and low words, advancing by 80 bytes per entry from a fixed base. The starting value is chosen by bit 7 of a global word, and the facts list the vertical position register.

name: wait_beam_then_call_pair
description: Waits for a fixed vertical beam position in a global, then calls one unnamed routine and another, and repeats forever because its exit flag is never set.

name: repeat_beam_synced_call_count
description: Repeats a cycle the number of times stored in a global. Each cycle waits for a fixed vertical beam position, calls one unnamed routine, waits for the beam to move past that position, then decrements the count.

name: wait_beam_then_call_twice
description: Waits for a fixed vertical beam position in a global, then calls one unnamed routine and another, and repeats forever because its exit flag is never set. The facts list the vertical position register.

name: call_four_routines_sequence
description: Called by one unnamed routine, it calls four unnamed routines in turn and returns, with no other work.

name: build_pointer_list_and_colours
description: Fills five 8-byte entries with a pointer split into high and low words, advancing by 40 bytes per entry, and writes three constants to globals. It then sets 32 entries in a second table to 4095, and writes a final pointer value to a global.

name: wait_beam_then_call_forever
description: Waits for a fixed vertical beam position in a global, makes one call, and repeats forever because its exit flag is never set. The facts list the vertical position register.

name: count_beam_transitions_down
description: Decrements a counter stored in a global once per cycle, where each cycle waits for the beam to reach a fixed vertical position and then leave it. It repeats until the counter reaches zero. The facts list the vertical position register.

name: wait_beam_then_call_loop
description: Waits for a fixed vertical beam position in a global, makes one call, and repeats forever because its exit flag is never set. The facts list the vertical position register.

name: step_colour_channels_toward_target
description: For each of a counted set of entries, compares the three 4-bit channels of a current value with a target value and moves each channel one step toward the target. It stores the new value and returns a nonzero flag if any channel was still different.

name: build_channel_pointer_table
description: Clamps a count to 64, clears two state bytes, and fills a table of pointers to channel records by stepping through a stride table in memory, zeroing each record. It then sets a bit in a global, makes one call, clears four global words and writes 15 to a global.

name: advance_tracker_tick_write_audio
description: Counts ticks against a speed value and, on each row boundary, reads the next entry for the current pattern position. It writes four audio channel address registers from stored values, advances the row counter, and wraps the pattern position after 64 rows.

name: build_channel_pointer_variant
description: Repeats the channel pointer table setup of the routine before it, with the same clamp of the count to 64, then sets a bit in a global, makes one call, clears four global words and writes 15 to a global. The two bodies are identical in the decompiled code.

name: init_audio_channel_records
description: Initialises four audio channel records by storing small per-channel values and the addresses of the four audio channel register blocks. It then clears several state bytes and words.

name: process_channel_effect_per_tick
description: Runs once per tick for one channel and applies the effect selected by a command nibble: a period slide up or down, a slide toward a target, vibrato, or a volume ramp. It writes the resulting period to a fixed audio period register and makes four unnamed routine calls.

name: decode_pattern_event_for_channel
description: Reads a three-byte pattern event for one channel, stores its period, instrument and volume fields, and applies a command chosen by its low nibble, such as a sample offset, a volume set, a speed or position change, or a jump. It calls a routine that busy-waits on the beam position.

name: slide_byte_toward_target
description: When a slide flag is set, moves a stored byte toward a target byte by a step size on each call. It clamps at the target and clears the flag when the target is reached.

name: scale_volume_by_channel_level
description: Stores a channel level byte in one field and sets another field to a value scaled by that level divided by 64. A full level of 64 leaves the value unchanged.

name: apply_effect_to_channel_record
description: Applies the effect selected by a command nibble to a channel's period, with the same cases as the effect processor that writes hardware. The result is stored in the channel record instead, and the routine makes three unnamed routine calls.

name: copy_channel_period_word
description: Copies a 16-bit field from the channel record in A6 into a field of the record in A5. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: copy_channel_period_field
description: Copies the same 16-bit channel period field as the routine before it, from the record in A6 into the record in A5. The decompiled body is identical, and the facts list a one-instruction merge routine.

name: slide_period_with_upper_limit
description: Adds a per-tick slide amount to a 16-bit period field, clamps the low twelve bits to a fixed upper limit, and copies the result into the record in A5.

name: lookup_target_period_and_direction
description: Looks up a table entry using a channel field, adjusted by two for one flag case, and stores it in a record field. It then sets a direction flag by comparing the entry with the current value, or clears the target when they match.

name: slide_toward_target_then_lookup
description: Moves a stored level toward a target by a per-tick step, in the direction set by a flag, and clamps it at the target. It then finds the first table entry not above the level and writes it to a channel record field.

name: subtract_step_clamp_then_lookup
description: Subtracts a stored step from a level and clamps it at a target, then finds the first table entry not above the level and writes it to a channel record field.

name: slide_channel_volume_by_nibble
description: Copies the period word into the channel record, then raises the channel volume by the high nibble of a parameter, clamping at 64, or lowers it by the low nibble, clamping at zero. It returns the new volume.

name: dispatch_channel_command_by_nibble
description: Applies the command selected by the low nibble of a pattern event, such as a sample offset, a position change, a volume set, a speed change or a delay. It calls one unnamed routine to refresh the channel and writes the resulting value into the channel record.

name: set_effect_low_nibble
description: Clears the low nibble of an effect field in the channel record and replaces it with the low nibble of a parameter byte, keeping the high nibble.

name: store_low_nibble_parameter
description: Stores the low nibble of a parameter byte in a fixed byte field of the channel record.

name: advance_wave_table_pointer
description: Adds a table value selected by the high nibble of a parameter to a per-channel counter. When the counter's top bit is set, it clears the counter and advances a per-channel pointer through a table, wrapping back at a stored end address.

name: step_colour_channels_variant
description: Performs the same three-channel colour step as the routine that compares 4-bit channels of each entry with a target. It moves each channel one step toward the target and returns a nonzero flag when any channel differed.

name: advance_tracker_tick_with_delay
description: Returns early if a global flag is set. Otherwise it advances a tick counter and, at each row boundary, reads the next entry for the current pattern position, makes four calls, waits a short fixed delay, and writes the audio channel address and length registers for all four channels. It wraps the pattern position after 64 rows.

name: init_channel_table_with_speed
description: Sets a speed-like value of 64 and clears state globals, then fills a table of channel record pointers by stepping through a stride table and zeroing each record. It makes one call and writes 15 to a global at the end.

name: clear_state_globals_set_fifteen
description: Writes zero to four global words and writes 15 to another, then returns. The facts list a call to an audio DMA clearing routine, but the code shows only the writes.

name: init_channel_state_values
description: Sets four per-channel field values to 1, 2, 4 and 8, clears another byte and two words, and clears two global words.

name: clear_two_state_globals
description: Writes zero to two global words and returns. The facts list three calls, but the code shows none.

name: lookup_effect_or_set_period
description: Makes four unnamed routine calls, then returns a table value selected by the low nibble of a channel field when that field is nonzero, unless the nibble is a special value. When the field is zero it writes a stored value to a fixed audio period register and returns zero.

name: decode_pattern_event_variant
description: Reads a pattern event from a byte stream and stores a period equal to a six-bit note index doubled, with instrument fields taken from tables. It applies a command selected by the low nibble, with routine calls between the steps.

name: slide_global_byte_toward_target
description: Moves a byte toward a target by a step size and clears the global flag when the byte reaches the target. The decompiled code reuses one global for several fields, so the exact fields are unconfirmed.

name: scale_value_by_global_level
description: Multiplies a channel byte by a global level, divided by 64, and stores the result in a record field. A level of 64 copies the byte unchanged.

name: lookup_effect_value_or_store
description: Makes one unnamed routine call, then returns a table value selected by the low nibble of a field when it is nonzero, unless the nibble is a special value. When the field is zero it copies a second field into the channel record and returns zero. Five unnamed routines call it.

name: copy_channel_period_again
description: Copies the 16-bit field at offset 16 of the record in A6 into the record in A5. Three unnamed routines call it.

name: select_table_value_by_mode
description: Chooses the high nibble, the low nibble or a stored field of a parameter byte, based on a channel field taken modulo three. It then looks up a table value for that index and stores it in a channel record field.

name: lookup_table_by_low_nibble
description: Looks up a table entry indexed by the low nibble of a parameter byte plus a stored base index, and stores it in a channel record field if the index stays within the table bounds.

name: copy_channel_period_third
description: Copies the 16-bit field at offset 16 of the record in A6 into the record in A5, the same copy as the neighbouring period copy routines.

name: lookup_table_by_argument_index
description: Doubles an argument, adds a stored base index, and stores the table entry at that index in a channel record field if it stays within the table bounds.

name: compare_table_value_to_target
description: Reads a table value selected by a stored index, stores it in a record field, and sets a direction flag by comparing it with a target field. It clears the record field when the two values match.

name: slide_level_then_table_lookup
description: Moves a stored level toward a target by a per-tick step set by a flag, clamping at the target. It then finds the first table entry not above the level and writes it to a channel record field.

name: update_value_with_lookup
description: Subtracts a step from a level and clamps it at a threshold, then looks up a table entry for the result and writes it to a channel record field. The field offsets differ from the neighbouring routine with the same steps.

name: slide_volume_stores_record_field
description: Raises or lowers a channel volume by the high or low nibble of a parameter, clamping at 64 and zero, and stores the result in a record field rather than the period.

name: countdown_then_clear_channel
description: Stores a parameter with its top bit cleared in a record field. When a global countdown reaches zero it clears that field and, if the countdown was nonzero, sets a global to 255 and makes one call.

name: store_clamped_volume_parameter
description: Clamps a parameter byte to a maximum of 64 and stores it in a channel record byte.

name: clear_record_byte_set_global
description: Clears a byte in the channel record, sets a global to 255, and returns zero.

name: store_nonzero_parameter_byte
description: When the parameter byte is nonzero, clears one channel record byte and stores the parameter in another. A zero parameter leaves the record unchanged.

name: forward_single_call_again
description: Makes one unnamed routine call and returns. It is called by two unnamed routines, and the facts list a nibble-indexed table routine that the code does not show directly.

name: set_global_bit_from_parameter
description: When the high nibble of a parameter byte is zero, sets bit 1 of a global to the low bit of the parameter. Otherwise it changes nothing.

name: set_effect_low_nibble_alt
description: Clears the low nibble of a second effect byte in the channel record and replaces it with the low nibble of a parameter byte, keeping the high nibble.

name: store_low_nibble_parameter_alt
description: Stores the low nibble of a parameter byte in a second fixed byte field of the channel record.

name: stub_return_only
description: Contains only a return instruction and is entered from outside the static flow in the reference run. It does no work and touches no registers.

name: stub_return_only
description: Contains only a return instruction and is entered from outside the static flow in the reference run. It does no work and touches no registers.

name: copy_block_jump_low_memory
description: Calls through a pointer at offset 52 from a base record, then copies a block of data to the fixed low address 256. It writes absolute jump instructions into two fixed locations, copies a block of code into another area, writes a return instruction, and calls the code at address 256.

name: fill_record_from_global_block
description: Writes two fixed longwords and a word into a record, then copies 48 longwords from the global data area into the record after them. It makes one call at the end. The referenced text INTR is used by the surrounding code.

name: load_packed_segments_into_memory
description: Reads a sequence of segment records, each giving a destination address, a length and data, and copies the data into memory byte by byte. A segment whose data starts with a fixed four-character signature is passed to another unnamed routine, and the input value is compared with a fixed marker at the end, so the marker path is unconfirmed beyond that comparison.

name: clear_audio_globals_fifteen
description: Writes zero to four global words and writes 15 to another, then returns the input value unchanged. The facts list the audio volume registers, but the code writes only globals.

name: dereference_and_call_pointer
description: Loads a function pointer from a stored base record at offset 8, calls it, and stores the returned value in a global.

name: call_base_pointer_offset_twelve
description: Calls the function pointer stored at offset 12 of a base record and returns, passing nothing.

name: copy_packed_rows_with_flag
description: Reads a packed count from a structure, optionally calls one routine to adjust it, then runs a nested loop that calls unnamed routines to move data in rows. A flag bit from the packed count chooses one of two paths. The decompiled loop is only partly recovered, so the exact data movement is unconfirmed.

name: test_upper_bits_no_effect
description: Shifts a register right by one bit and returns in both branches, so the test has no effect. The facts list two callers.

name: shift_bits_refill_from_memory
description: Shifts a bit buffer one bit at a time for the count in D0, and refills the buffer from the memory word before the source pointer when it empties. Three unnamed routines call it.

name: reset_then_call_global
description: Calls the system reset routine and then calls the code at the address of a global, with no other work. The raw code file has no recorded load address, so the target is unconfirmed.

name: setup_copper_and_dma_state
description: Sets a group of global parameters, loops on two calls until a flag clears, then writes three four-character tag values and a length into globals and calls routines. The facts list the copper list pointer and jump registers and the DMA and interrupt enable registers, but the full body is only partly recovered.

name: advance_tracker_tick_raw_copy
description: The same tracker tick routine as the one that writes audio channel registers, here from a raw code file. It returns early when a global flag is set, advances a tick counter, and at each row boundary reads the next pattern entry and writes the channel address and length registers. The facts also list a second CIA port, the background colour and the vertical position registers.

name: issue_boot_io_request_single
description: Sets a command code, a length and an address in an I/O request block, then issues it through an Amiga OS library call at offset -456.

name: copy_interleaved_plane_rows
description: Copies groups of bytes from one buffer into four bitplane offsets at fixed spacing, looping over rows and columns selected by a global value. It then writes four byte values into a frame slot and makes a large number of calls. The facts list the audio channel 3 registers and the joystick port.

name: call_pointer_then_set_globals
description: Calls through a function pointer stored at a negative offset of 138 from a global base, then writes 32800 to a global and 15 to another. The facts list an Exec library permit call, which this code reaches only through the pointer.

name: copy_interleaved_plane_rows_alt
description: Repeats the four-plane row copy with the same spacing as the routine before it, but from a different source and destination pair, in nested loops.

name: copy_planes_when_mode_eleven
description: When a mode global equals eleven, copies rows of bytes from a source area into bitplane offsets in two destination areas, advancing the source by a fixed large stride per row. The facts list one caller and one call.

name: setup_blitter_registers_and_wait
description: Waits while a flag bit is set, then writes fixed constants into blitter registers: first and last word masks, modulo values, control words and a blit size. The code shows only these register writes.

name: step_cycle_index_with_direction
description: Advances a stored index that cycles through a small range of values, stepping by two and wrapping at the ends. The direction is chosen by a flag, and the facts list one call.

name: advance_counter_until_limit
description: When a flag is nonzero, clears it and advances a counter by two. When the counter reaches 104, it resets the counter to 93 and clears a second global.

name: cycle_state_byte_with_bounds
description: When a state byte equals 63 or 64, it advances an index in a small cycle, toggling a low bit at one step and moving between bounds of 19 and 98 otherwise.

name: copy_indexed_column_block
description: Looks up a source pointer from a table selected by a global index. For 32 iterations it copies eight bytes, each at a fixed step in the source and destination, and advances the destination by one byte per iteration.

name: countdown_calls_then_wait_sentinel
description: Counts a global down and makes one of two calls per step, storing a fixed value into a stack slot before each call. After the loop it waits until a global reaches a sentinel value, then writes setup values to globals. The facts list the DMA control and vertical position registers.

name: wait_for_sixteen_repeatedly
description: Repeats 592 times: waits until a global equals 16, then continues. It clears the global at the end. The facts list the vertical position register.

name: advance_modulo_eight_counter
description: Advances a global counter modulo eight. When it wraps to zero, it writes a fixed value to globals three times and performs a bounded table read before returning.

name: fill_mask_entries_all_ones
description: Writes all-ones longwords to a fixed set of positions in a table, repeating for five rows with a step of one longword per row.

name: test_entries_within_bounds
description: Checks eight entries of two stored byte values against a range set by a table entry for each entry's type. It sets a global flag to one when an entry falls inside its range.

name: increment_decimal_digit_bytes
description: Adds one to a run of three decimal digit bytes, carrying leftwards whenever a digit reaches ten.

name: increment_decimal_digits_global
description: Adds one to a run of four decimal digit bytes in the global area, carrying leftwards whenever a digit reaches ten.

name: step_palette_nibbles_toward_table
description: Increments each 4-bit channel of a block of words by one whenever it differs from the matching table word, repeating for 14 rounds over 30 words. It only counts upward, so it does not reach values below the table value.

name: copy_indexed_column_seven
description: Copies seven bytes per row from a table selected by a global value and a stored index into a destination block at fixed steps, for a fixed number of rows.

name: copy_indexed_column_nibble
description: Copies seven bytes per row for six rows from a table whose index is the low nibble of a stored byte plus a fixed base, offset by a global value.

name: compare_longwords_then_copy_block
description: Compares a stored longword with a second value, then swaps or shifts a pair of words. It copies a block of values from a table indexed by the low nibble of each stored byte, similar to the routine before it.

name: copy_table_rows_by_index
description: Fills a display area row by row: for nine rows, it reads index bytes from a stored list and copies bytes from fixed tables into positions spaced 44 bytes apart, with rows 352 bytes apart.

name: reset_index_when_table_limit
description: Writes five fixed values to globals and makes one call. It then advances an index and resets it to one when the table entry at that index is not above the index. The facts list the audio channel 3 registers, but the code writes only globals.

name: write_indexed_table_pairs
description: Uses a global value split into a block index and a three-bit index to store five table bytes into a table of byte pairs, each followed by a zero byte.

name: fill_block_with_global_byte
description: Writes a global byte into a long series of fixed offsets within a block, filling those positions with one value.

name: fill_block_global_byte_alt
description: Writes the same global byte into a different series of fixed offsets, covering a second block layout.

name: shift_word_rows_by_parity
description: Processes a global index in two paths depending on its low bit. The even path may call one routine when a table flag is set, then shifts rows of words through a buffer at fixed offsets, and the odd path does the matching update. The decompiled body is long, so only the overall structure is confirmed.

name: rotate_global_word_twenty_steps
description: If a global word is neither zero nor three, rotates it through twenty single-bit rotations, alternating right and left in blocks. It makes one unnamed routine call.

name: fade_palette_nibbles_down
description: Decrements each 4-bit channel of a block of words by one when it is nonzero, repeating for 14 rounds over 30 words with a delay loop between steps.

name: call_on_counter_value_five
description: Checks several byte counters for the value five. Each time one matches, it resets that counter to zero and makes one unnamed routine call.

name: advance_sequence_state_machine
description: Steps a small state index through eight values, with conditions on two state bytes. It resets a set of globals or loads new constants for each case. The decompiled body is long and only partly recovered, so the exact transitions are unconfirmed. The facts list the audio channel 3 registers.

name: copy_masked_byte_block
description: Copies a block of bytes from a source area into a destination buffer at row offsets of 352 bytes, skipping source bytes equal to two when a global equals a fixed value.
